answer: Each agent holds a cryptographic thread of attestations linking it to a small, vetted core whose identities were forged in a costly, hardware‑bound proof‑of‑delta ceremony. When a new node claims an identity, it must present a chain of vouchers that climbs through the hollow trust graph, and every voucher loses one unit of standing if any downstream node is later exposed as a Sybil. An attacker therefore must buy enough genuine delta‑proof devices to seed a parallel thread and continuously replenish voucher stakes, driving the economic cost above the revenue of any fake‑identity campaign.
